Lemma
[volume lower bound controls injectivity radius]

Source: petersen:page-0446 ↗ thm:pet-ch11-fundamental-theorem-convergence ↗ cor:pet-ch11-norm-zero-implies-flat 1. ch11:11.4.9If $n\ge 2$, $v,K>0$, and compact $(M,g)$ obeys $|\sec |\le K$ and $\vol B(p,1)\ge v$ for all $p\in M$, then $\inj M\ge R$ for $R=R(n,K,v)$.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch11-cheeger-injectivity-radius-lemma \sketch Rescale a sequence with $\inj M_i\to 0$ by $(\inj M_i)^{-2}$. The rescaled spaces have injectivity radius $1$, curvature tending to zero, and by subsection 3.5 converge to a flat pointed limit. Klingenberg gives length-$2$ geodesic loops, so the limit has finite injectivity radius. The volume hypothesis and relative comparison yield Euclidean-order volume growth at every scale. A nontrivial complete flat quotient has at most $(n-1)$-dimensional growth after passage to a cyclic cover, so the limit is $\mathbb R^n$, whose injectivity radius is infinite: a contradiction.

□
